_purpose: The operation registry: what can actually be CALLED, with the call path, the parameters, the inputs/outputs, the applicable scope and the evidence for each. The four capability levels are deliberately separate (AGENTS.md section 1 and the R11 instruction): a real call path, verification on the CURRENT case, general acceptance, and engineering validity. Nothing here claims the last one.
_availability_rule: `implementation` is NEVER read from this file: scripts/casespec.py resolves every entry against the live workflow catalog and the files on disk, and an entry whose stage, macro or script is missing is reported as UNRESOLVED and can never make a plan executable.

capability_levels.implementation: a real call path resolves: stage in workflows/<id>/manifest.json with its macros on disk, or a named tool/script that exists
capability_levels.verified_on_current_case: the evidence below names this case AND the record is certified by scripts/run_record_gate.py; a record from a FAILED run never counts
capability_levels.general_acceptance: GENERAL_OPERATION (representative positive AND negative), TRIALED_POSITIVE_AND_NEGATIVE, TRIALED_POSITIVE, COMPILED_ONLY, or NOT_ACCEPTED (sample-specific)
capability_levels.engineering: ALWAYS NOT_CLAIMED_BY_WIRING: wiring an operation proves it runs, never that the physics is valid

workflow_stage.description: one STAR stage of an installed workflow manifest, submitted through the formal MCP path
workflow_stage.runner: worker/run_pipeline.ps1 -> worker/run_job.ps1 (one STAR process per macro, macro_outputs chaining)
workflow_stage.runner_hash_layers: TWO layers, TWO reviewed hashes (R12): `pipeline_runner_sha256` is verified by worker/run_pipeline.ps1 against its own $PSCommandPath, and `runner_sha256` by worker/run_job.ps1 against its own. Passing one hash for both layers is the defect that refused every formal stage; backend.RUNNER_REVIEW_FIELDS holds the mapping and a record must pin both for submit_run.
workflow_stage.parameter_channel: each step carries `env`; the runner sets only the declared names for its own child processes and records them in the stage record
workflow_stage.verified_output: mcp report_run(run_id, evidence, case_label) / scripts/formal_run_report.py: retrieves the run, re-hashes every artifact against the runner's recorded sha256 and calls scripts/generate_run_report.py unchanged
workflow_stage.review: scripts/backend.py::load_review_record compares pipeline/controller/each runner layer/macro/input hashes before submission, and worker/run_job.ps1 recomputes its own on Windows

offline_tool.description: a Mac-side tool or the runner records; no STAR process of its own
offline_tool.entry: the named MCP tool or script
offline_tool.plan_coverage_rule: R12: an offline tool completes a plan step only through an `invoked_by` entry whose file and symbol really exist on disk (casespec._code_bindings). `applies_to_run_mechanisms` is display-only: a declaration that nothing calls must not complete a plan.

restricted_trial.description: a whole reviewed pipeline driven by the branch-1 trial entry; the verified execution mechanism for scenarios 1-3

operations.inputs: a HyperMesh native quality record (JSON): tool name/version, source file+sha256, mesh file+sha256/dimension/element_count/units (plus optional dimension_counts), and one entry per native criterion (*elementtestaspect/skew/jacobian) carrying command, short label, threshold, direction, units, checked count, failed count, worst value, and - whenever failed>0 - the bad-element localization (output mark, failed element IDs, per-element values, coordinates); the record must also declare localization_complete and per_cell_values_saved as booleans, and - whenever any criterion fails - mesh.element_id_bounds [lo, hi] so the failed IDs can be shown to belong to this mesh, because a run whose per-cell check values were not saved cannot be admitted even when every criterion passes
outputs: an admission verdict (RECORD_INCOMPLETE / LOCALIZATION_MISSING / FAILED_CRITERIA_WITH_LOCALIZATION / ADMITTED) plus reasons, per-criterion facts and repair_targets for a targeted HyperMesh-side fix
operations.scope: Offline, fail-closed admission judge for the HyperMesh NATIVE quality gate only. It never claims STAR or CFD admission: star_admitted / cfd_admitted / engineering_verified are always False in its verdict (AGENTS.md section 8 - the two tools' metrics do not substitute for each other). Its other output is the honest boundary of what a failure means: a record without bad-element localization cannot be cited as a HyperMesh capability gap.
operations.applicable_when: any case whose mesh was checked with HyperMesh native element checks (*elementtestaspect / *elementtestskew / *elementtestjacobian and hm_getelemcheckvalues) before any STAR import
operations.positive: a complete record whose every criterion passes with per-cell values saved AND localization_complete=true is admitted for the next INDEPENDENT stage; verdict.quality_admitted=true while star_admitted/cfd_admitted/engineering_verified stay false (tests/test_hypermesh_quality_gate.py::PassingAndIncomplete)
operations.negative: the same real repair2 numbers fed to the gate TWO ways: the actual file (test-evidence/finite-trailing-edge-policy-20261014/hypermesh-native2d-surface-repair2-preparation/quality_gate.json) carries aggregate fields only, so the gate returns RECORD_INCOMPLETE on it; a record rebuilt from those numbers returns LOCALIZATION_MISSING with can_claim_hypermesh_capability_gap=false. Further negatives: wrong number of IDs, duplicate/non-positive IDs, an ID outside mesh.element_id_bounds, missing per-element value, missing coordinate, a criterion that covered only part of the mesh, a declared dimension covered by no criterion (independent review D-1), non-finite worst, status=ok with failures, and a record claiming cfd_admitted/star_admitted true
operations.registration_basis: Registered as TRIALED_POSITIVE_AND_NEGATIVE for the JUDGE ITSELF - an offline pure function with a positive fixture, a REAL negative fixture and mutant negatives, exercised by tests/test_hypermesh_quality_gate.py and by the independent adversarial suite test-evidence/hypermesh-mesh-tooling-policy-20261014/independent_review_tests.py. This entry deliberately carries NO evidence[] array: no case-bound certificate exists, so nothing here can make verified_on_current_case true. This is NOT an acceptance of any HyperMesh execution: invoked_by is empty, plan_role is absent (so it contributes no capability to any mechanism coverage and cannot complete a required plan step, measured), and the mesh-generation/check/repair route on Windows stays unaccepted until a localized native quality record exists.
operations.open_gap: C-3 (independent review): no consumer calls this gate yet. Until the STAR-side preparation step invokes assert_admissible before an external mesh is imported, the single judge is a written rule plus an offline tool, not an enforced gate in any pipeline. Separately (review R2-7, measured by the parent): naming this id in plan_operations is ACCEPTED (the resolver lists it among the selected plan operations) but it contributes NO capability to any mechanism coverage - validate_case_spec on the scenario-1 fixture reports plan_unresolved=[] and the capability hypermesh_quality_admission does not appear in mechanism_coverage, with or without the id named. It therefore cannot complete a required plan step; the earlier wording claimed more than that.
